speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) in the past three years, what has been the progress of developing more Information and Technology (IT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) professionals under the Career Conversion Programme; and (b) what is the Ministry’s plan in further developing this in the next three to five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: These include the more than 1,300 artificial intelligence (AI)-related courses offered by SkillsFuture Singapore as well as career conversion programmes supported by Workforce Singapore, which may also help Singaporeans take up jobs requiring AI-related skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: These initiatives complement our broader efforts to expand the pipeline of AI practitioners, including enhancing the AI-readiness of information and digital technology (IDT) graduates from our Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Our industry partners have also initiated programmes to train and hire AI practitioners, such as AI Singapore's AI Apprenticeship programme, Singtel's Catalyst programme and Temus’ Step IT Up programme.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can I have a couple of supplementary questions?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I want to ask whether they have plans to increase these conversion programmes, in terms of the frequency of the programmes and the number of programmes?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The number 190 compared to 5,000, is quite a far cry.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: How have the private sectors chipped in and how many mid-career professionals have they converted to become AI professionals?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It may be useful for me to set the context of the figures that he has cited.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In December 2023, we launched the refreshed National AI Strategy 2.0, which sets out our vision and plans to achieve AI for the public good for Singapore and the world.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To support this ambition, we intend to expand our pool of AI practitioners and uplift our workforce to be confident AI users.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will look to re-skilling and upskilling our locals to take on these roles.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To develop the additional 10,000 AI practitioners, we are looking at a few approaches.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, these are for pre-employment training, or PET.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: About 10,000, 5,000 will be through the PET route.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, that is the context of the figures of 10,000 and 5,000, which the Member cited.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the 5,000 CET number, a recent Estimates Committee report noted that the CCP has, so far, only helped 190 people transit in their new roles.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Allow me to set in context the 190 figure that Parliament's Estimates Committee referred to.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: JTM is Job Transformation Map for the information and communication workforce, which was published in October 2022.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That JTM report identified AI as one of the key emerging trends that will transform technology roles.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) partnered with five JTM partners to scale reskilling and upskilling efforts in AI and analytics, with an emphasis on generative AI (Gen AI) and two other in-demand areas: software engineering and cloud and mobility.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We launched the JTM Partners Programme and we are making good progress with our JTM partners since it launched in 2023, last year.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, the 190 figure was in the context of that very specific JTM training programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But as I mentioned earlier in my reply, we have a suite of different programmes under TeSA and under CCP which have shown good results in the past.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: JTM is part of this umbrella of effort that the Government is doing and there are many industry partners – I mentioned some in my earlier reply – and they are also stepping up to support mid-career transitions, supporting people who are currently in IT roles or technology roles to pick up new certifications, new skills to do new AI roles that are emerging.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I would also like to share with the Member that besides the good progress we are making with the JTM partners, we have a healthy pipeline of workers who have expressed interest to undergo the necessary CCP training.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In summary, the figures that the Estimates Committee referred to, the 190, is set in context to the specific JTM programme, which is part of the broader career conversion and TeSA skills that we are doing and part of the broader AI talent manpower strategy that we have embarked on.
